name: AlUla Old Town and Al Jadidah
tagline: The restored mudbrick quarter and the arts district beside it
description: The old town is a labyrinth of restored mudbrick houses below the citadel, and Al Jadidah next to it has become the valley's dining and arts district, with galleries, cafes and small hotels along a pedestrian strip. It is the most atmospheric part of the whole area.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to walk to dinner rather than drive to it
pros: The only genuinely walkable part of the valley
Best concentration of restaurants and cafes
Restored heritage architecture at the door
cons: Accommodation is boutique and priced accordingly
Very busy during the winter season
Almost nothing open in the summer months

name: Ashar Valley
tagline: The resort valley among the sandstone outcrops
description: A canyon north of the town where most of the high-end accommodation sits, including the mirrored Maraya concert hall that hosts the winter programme. The setting among sheer sandstone walls is extraordinary and the pricing matches it exactly.
bestFor: Short high-budget stays built around the winter season events
pros: The most striking setting in the valley
Maraya and the concert programme nearby
Best service and internet in the area
cons: The most expensive accommodation in Saudi Arabia
Isolated, so every meal is on site or a drive
Books out entirely during the winter season

name: AlUla Town Centre
tagline: The modern town where people actually live
description: The functional part of AlUla along the main road, with supermarkets, ordinary restaurants, the hospital and the housing that the resident population and the project workforce use. It is unglamorous and it is where any stay longer than a week becomes affordable.
bestFor: Longer stays where the daily costs matter more than the view
pros: Central to the whole valley by car
cons: No character and little to look at
Still requires a car for everything

name: The Oasis Strip
tagline: Date palms along the valley floor
description: The band of palm groves and farm plots running the length of the valley below the old town, irrigated for millennia and still worked. A few farmstay-style properties have opened among them, and the shaded walking paths through the palms are the coolest place in AlUla.
bestFor: Anyone wanting shade, quiet and a working landscape
pros: Genuine shade, which is scarce here
Quiet and green in a desert valley
cons: Still a drive from the restaurants
